preamble: Spirantization of a uvular stop to a velar fricative. The documented case is Georgian: the Old Georgian uvular stop written ჴ (qar), described as /qʰ/ or /q/, merged with the velar fricative ხ /x/, and the letter ჴ fell out of use (ჴელი qeli > ხელი xeli 'hand', ჴმაჲ qmay > ხმა xma 'voice'). Modern Georgian /x/ is itself often pronounced post-velar to uvular. The Mingrelian cognate ხუმა 'voice' is given with uvular [χ] and Turkic q > χ spirantization also produces a uvular fricative; both belong to the q > χ cell.

examples.note: Old Georgian uvular ჴ merged with velar ხ /x/ (phonetically ranging from velar to uvular depending on context). The atlas has no separate aspirated-uvular symbol, so the change is filed under q.

examples.to: Modern Georgian ხმა xma 'voice, sound; vote'
examples.note: Inherited from Proto-Georgian-Zan *qam-, *qm-; Old Georgian ჴ is replaced by ხ in the modern spelling.
